passages.note: Bill details page lists Wesco as a House sponsor of SB 101 and shows it was signed into law.
House Roll Call 305 shows Wesco among the 63 Yea votes on SB 101's 3rd reading, a single-subject bill.

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled act text creates a claim/defense allowing religious exemptions from government burdens absent strict scrutiny.

rows.reasoning: Wesco was a House sponsor of SB 101 (2015), Indiana's RFRA, and voted Yea on its single-subject final passage (Roll Call 305). The enrolled act bars government from substantially burdening religious exercise absent a compelling interest pursued by the least restrictive means, and lets a person assert that as a claim or defense against conflicting laws, matching the rung text 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs.'
